content: It is specifically used in individuals whose daily activities are significantly impaired by this condition, even after trying other treatments such as support stockings. To use this medication, take it orally with or without food as directed by your doctor, typically three times daily, ensuring at least 3 to 4 hours between doses. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. Midodrine is taken during daytime hours when standing is most frequent. It should not be taken after the evening meal or within four hours of bedtime. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose and gradually increase it to minimize side effects. Regular use is essential to achieve the maximum benefit. Inform your doctor if your condition persists or worsens. Common side effects may include skin tingling, chills, goosebumps, stomach pain, or urinary issues such as a strong or frequent urge to urinate, frequent urination, or difficulty urinating. Less common side effects include dry mouth, dizziness, drowsiness, trouble sleeping, or leg cramps. Remember, this medication is prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare but possible. Before taking midodrine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Rarely, this medication may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Midodrine should not be used during pregnancy as it may harm an unborn baby. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Share these results with your doctor. Additionally, laboratory and medical tests, such as kidney and liver function tests, should be conducted while taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
